text:
Muscle lactate production increases when glycolysis outpaces the mitochondria's ability to oxidize pyruvate. That happens in intense exercise or when oxygen is limited, and the resulting lactate regenerates NAD⁺. Neither option in the team note fits: "oxygen is readily available" is the opposite of the real trigger, and lactate forms from pyruvate, so it can't rise when pyruvate "cannot be formed." If I had to pick, I'd lean toward the second, but I think the note's options are wrong or incomplete.

CONFIDENCE: 55
